lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: angles of elevation and depression

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A 3-4-5 triangle, θ opposite the side 3. Find sin θ.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 24 and 45. Find the hypotenuse.
Express sin 66° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 66°, because sine and cosine are always equal
cos 114°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 156°, because the angles differ by a right angle
cos 24°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent

items.prompt: From a point 45 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 24 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 10 and 24 and hypotenuse 26. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 10. Find cos θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse 20 and one leg 12. Find the other leg.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
